issues.description: The problem statement and UML require the constructor parameters to follow the attribute order (lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents, numberOfGuestStudents, numberOfLecturers, numberOfTutors). The solution's Lecture constructor uses a different parameter order (lectureName, numberOfLecturers, numberOfTutors, numberOfInscribedStudents, numberOfGuestStudents). This mismatch can confuse students about the expected constructor signature and will break exercises/tests that check parameter order.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the constructor parameter order with the UML and problem description. Change the constructor signature to: public Lecture(String lectureName, int numberOfInscribedStudents, int numberOfGuestStudents, int numberOfLecturers, int numberOfTutors) and assign fields accordingly. Alternatively, if the solution order was intentional, update the problem statement/UML to reflect the chosen parameter order so all artifacts match.

issues.description: The Lecture constructor parameter order in the solution does not follow the order specified in the problem statement / UML. The problem / UML lists attributes in the order: lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents, numberOfGuestStudents, numberOfLecturers, numberOfTutors and instructs the constructor to follow this order. The solution implements the constructor as (String lectureName, int numberOfLecturers, int numberOfTutors, int numberOfInscribedStudents, int numberOfGuestStudents). This mismatch between the expected constructor parameter order and the solution's constructor can confuse students mapping requirements to implementation and may lead to incorrectly passed arguments or failing constructor-related tests.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the Lecture constructor parameter order with the UML/problem statement. Use: public Lecture(String lectureName, int numberOfInscribedStudents, int numberOfGuestStudents, int numberOfLecturers, int numberOfTutors) and assign each parameter to the corresponding field in the same order. Update the template and solution to use this constructor signature so students can directly map requirements to the implementation.
